title: Negative possession with plural owners
summary: Build plural-owner negative possession statements: owner + ei ole + partitive thing.
prerequisiteSkills: Regular singular partitive in negative possession
objectives: Build plural-owner negative possession statements: owner + ei ole + partitive thing.
Apply the pattern using the supporting forms shown.

sections.title: How the pattern works
paragraphs: Build plural-owner negative possession statements: owner + ei ole + partitive thing.
Choose meillä, teillä, and heillä. Keep ei and ole together after the owner, then use the complete partitive noun shown or learned.
keyPoints: Build plural-owner negative possession statements: owner + ei ole + partitive thing.

examples.english: We do not have a dog.
steps: Begin with the owner meillä. meillä means “we as the owner”.
Place ei ole next as the two-word negative possession frame.
Finish with the learned partitive koiraa (“a dog”): owner + ei + ole + thing.

examples.english: You do not have a book.
steps: Begin with the owner teillä. teillä means “you as the owner” for a group.
Place ei ole next as the two-word negative possession frame.
Finish with the learned partitive kirjaa (“a book”): owner + ei + ole + thing.

examples.english: They do not have a cat.
steps: Begin with the owner heillä. heillä means “they as the owner”.
Place ei ole next as the two-word negative possession frame.
Finish with the learned partitive kissaa (“a cat”): owner + ei + ole + thing.

examples.english: You do not have a pillow.
steps: Begin with the owner teillä. teillä means “you as the owner” for a group.
Place ei ole next as the two-word negative possession frame.
Finish with the learned partitive tyynyä (“a pillow”): owner + ei + ole + thing.

examples.english: We do not have a pen.
steps: meillä identifies the plural owner in this negative possession with plural owners pattern.
Use owner + ei ole; possession keeps the verb pattern fixed.
kynää (“a pen”) is the complete regular singular partitive: kynä + -ä.

examples.english: You do not have a game.
steps: teillä identifies the plural owner in this negative possession with plural owners pattern.
Use owner + ei ole; possession keeps the verb pattern fixed.
peliä (“a game”) is the complete regular singular partitive: peli + -ä.

commonMistakes: Keep the requested order: owner + ei ole + partitive noun. Do not leave out ole.

practiceExercises.prompt: Optional practice: Translate “Heillä ei ole palloa.” into English.
acceptedAnswers: They do not have a ball.
They do not have the ball.
practiceExercises.explanation: The -lla/-llä phrase identifies the owner; ei ole stays fixed in this possession pattern.
requiredSkills: Regular singular partitive in negative possession
practiceExercises.misconceptionCategory: Negative possession sentences: form or meaning confused

sentenceExplanation.translation: They do not have a ball.
sentenceExplanation.pattern: possessor + fixed ei ole + singular partitive noun

parts.role: possessor: the person who has the thing
parts.formation: he has the learned possession form heillä; its -lla/-llä ending marks the possessor. Learn this pronoun form as a whole.
Possession uses fixed ei with meillä, teillä and heillä; do not change it to emme, ette or eivät.
After ei, olla uses ole. Together ei ole means “do not have” or “does not have” here.
pallo + -a = palloa. This is the singular partitive, the noun form used when possession is denied.
